newsitem.title: RUSSIA: No effect from Russia gems committee move - De Beers.
newsitem.headline: No effect from Russia gems committee move - De Beers.

text.p: De Beers said on Friday a Russian decree dividing the powers of a state diamond agency between two ministries had not affected ongoing negotiations but said it did not know what the effects of the move would be.
"We have not been affected by any of the changes thus far. I honestly don't know what the result will be," said Raymond Clarke, head of De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd's Moscow representation.
Clarke said De Beers had ongoing relationships with a number of federal officials, including some at the finance ministry.
"The finance ministry has been responsible for a large stockpile of diamonds, some of which we have bought over the years," he said.

A finance ministry spokesman said a presidential decree of August 14 called for the duties of the Russian Committee for Precious Metals and Stones (Komdragmet) to be divided between the finance and industry ministries.
"Normative acts being worked on will clarify which (duties) go to the finance ministry and which to the industry ministry," the spokesman said.

De Beers is conducting negotiations, set to resume on September 3, with Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS), Russia's largest diamond producer and sole exporter, which is owned in part by the Russian government.
Clarke said any agreements by ARS would have faced broad approval by the government in any case.
"Although they have been appointed to conduct negotiations, any final decision would be subject to the scrutiny of a number of bodies, including, formerly, Komdragmet," Clarke said.
